result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian infrastructure including signals and marked crosswalks, but the environment is dominated by wide asphalt surfaces and lacks physical protection. Sidewalks are present but appear poorly maintained, and the overall design prioritizes vehicle throughput over pedestrian comfort.

hazards.name: Wide turning radius
hazards.description: The corner geometry allows for high-speed vehicle turns, increasing risk to pedestrians at the crossing.

hazards.name: Faded crosswalk markings
hazards.description: The zebra markings are somewhat worn, reducing visibility to approaching drivers.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked vehicles
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection may block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street beyond the crosswalk

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and slow turning traffic.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install or upgrade curb ramps with tactile warning pads to ensure accessibility for all users.

result.summary: The intersection features a marked zebra crosswalk and pedestrian signals, but is cluttered with utility poles and overhead wires. Visibility is compromised by vehicles parked close to the crossing, and the pavement surface is significantly degraded.

hazards.name: Utility Pole Obstruction
hazards.description: A large utility pole is located directly in the pedestrian path at the corner, narrowing the accessible space.

hazards.name: Poor Sight Lines
hazards.description: Parked vehicles are positioned very close to the crosswalk, obstructing the view between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image, near the crosswalk

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: The roadway surface within and around the crosswalk is cracked and uneven, posing a trip hazard.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and prevent parking too close to the intersection.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve visibility for all road users.

interventions.title: Pavement Resurfacing
interventions.description: Repair the cracked and degraded roadway to provide a smooth, safe crossing surface.

result.summary: The street features a marked zebra crosswalk and sidewalks on both sides, but lacks active traffic control or signage. Parked vehicles right up to the crossing create significant visual obstructions for both pedestrians and drivers, and the pavement within the crosswalk is visibly degraded.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles are located immediately adjacent to the crosswalk, blocking sightlines between pedestrians and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and right sides of the foreground crosswalk

hazards.name: Degraded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The zebra markings are worn and the pavement is cracked, reducing the visibility and clarity of the pedestrian zone.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces within 20 feet of the crosswalk to improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the crossing to shorten the crossing distance and physically prevent parking too close to the intersection.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signage
interventions.description: Install high-visibility pedestrian crossing warning signs to alert drivers to the presence of the crosswalk.

result.summary: The intersection features marked zebra crosswalks and ADA-compliant curb ramps with tactile paving. However, the environment lacks dedicated pedestrian signals and street trees, and parked vehicles near the corner may obstruct sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection corner can block the line of sight between pedestrians waiting to cross and approaching motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image along the curb line

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The zebra-style crosswalk markings show signs of wear and fading, which reduces their visibility to drivers.

hazards.name: Degraded Road Surface
hazards.description: Cracking and minor potholes in the asphalt near the crosswalk area could present a tripping hazard or affect vehicle braking.
hazards.location_in_image: Roadway surface within and near the crosswalk

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to reduce the pedestrian crossing distance and improve visibility by moving pedestrians past the line of parked cars.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Repainting
interventions.description: Refresh the crosswalk markings with high-visibility thermoplastic to ensure they are clearly seen by approaching traffic.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information on crossing time remaining.
